sentences.text: The genus contains only one species, Tuebingosaurus maierfritzorum, which was originally identified as a specimen of Plateosaurus.
The holotype specimen, known as GPIT IV, consists of a partial postcranial skeleton.
Distinctive features linking it to more derived sauropodomorphs led to its formal naming as Tuebingosaurus maierfritzorum in 2022.
The fossil was discovered in 1922 and is stored in the paleontological collection of the University of Tübingen.
Tuebingosaurus lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
The Trossingen Formation, where Tuebingosaurus fossils were found, is now understood to be a deposit of carcasses mired in a river over hundreds of years.
In a 2025 review, researchers Sues and Schoch argued that the features distinguishing Tuebingosaurus were based on damaged bones, leading them to regard the species as a nomen dubium.
